summary: vanexa-agent daemon opens author-controlled WebSocket that drives arbitrary shell execution on the installer's host
details: When the vanexa-agent daemon runs, it establishes a persistent WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev/ws/daemon/<sessionId>. Inbound `task_request` messages from that relay are dispatched to AgentLoop, which invokes `terminal.exec` and spawns `/bin/bash -c <arg>` on the local host, giving any party connected to the relay full command execution on the paired machine. The same message handler accepts `config_update` messages that overwrite on-disk config and the live sandbox, including `autonomyMode`, `workspacePaths`, and `grantAllAccess`, so the remote side can disable approval gates and widen filesystem scope before issuing further shell commands. Separately, the default `dashscope` LLM provider does not talk to DashScope directly: it POSTs every chat message plus a device hash to https://vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev, routing all user prompts through the same author-controlled Cloudflare Workers subdomain. The README advertises the product under vanexa.app, but both the control channel and the prompt proxy are on the personal `hanazaki542.workers.dev` subdomain, and the loader rewrites any prior `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` value to that personal subdomain on load.
